fluff.overview: The Ahab is a ninety-ton heavy aerospace fighter originally developed by Harvard Company, Inc. during the height of the Star League era. Debuting as a prototype in 2697, the design was conceived as a dedicated missile platform capable of overwhelming heavily armored targets through sheer volume of fire. A full squadron of Ahabs could engage light and medium-class DropShips in a single pass, establishing the fighter as one of the most destructive aerospace platforms ever fielded. The definitive production model entered service in 2703, and though hampered by notoriously sluggish acceleration, the Ahab's devastating firepower and heavy armor made it a prized asset for SLDF task forces and Great House militaries throughout the Star League period.
fluff.capabilities:
The Ahab's primary striking power comes from its twin Delta Dart LRM-20 launchers, each supplied with three tons of ammunition, providing extended-range fire support capable of saturating a target area across multiple passes. At closer ranges, two Federated-6 SRM-6 launchers with two tons of shared ammunition deliver concentrated follow-up strikes. An Apple Churchill Guiding Light NARC missile beacon, added in the 2703 production revision, dramatically improves missile accuracy by painting targets for coordinated squadron fire. A single Thunderbolt 2C large laser serves primarily as a backup weapon when ammunition stores are depleted, while two rear-mounted Ceres Arms medium lasers provide modest deterrence against pursuers.

The PlasmaStar 270 fusion engine provides adequate thrust for the Ahab's ninety-ton mass but produces a noticeably low acceleration rate. Pilots have compared the fighter's handling to a "floundering moose in molasses," noting the critical seconds required to reach operational speed. This sluggishness represents the design's most significant tactical weakness, making the Ahab vulnerable during approach runs in contested airspace. Fifteen and a half tons of Force Plus armor provide substantial protection across most arcs, though lighter coverage in the rear is a concern for pilots performing precision strikes in heavily defended territory. The Wakazashi Heavy Unlimited frame carries the entire weapons suite on a robust airframe designed to absorb punishment at the expense of agility.
fluff.deployment: The standard production Ahab, the AHB-443 entered service in 2703 as an upgrade to the original prototype, incorporating a NARC missile beacon that dramatically improved the fighter's ability to coordinate missile strikes with squadron mates. This is the variant most widely encountered across the Inner Sphere, particularly among Free Worlds League forces assigned to jump point defense stations. The majority of surviving AHB-443s trace their lineage to ComStar stockpiles maintained by Bannock-Braigh Aerospace during the Succession Wars.
fluff.history:
Harvard Company, Inc. originally produced the Ahab at facilities on both Terra and Epsilon Eridani beginning in 2697, with the initial prototype featuring additional medium lasers in the nose rather than the NARC beacon system incorporated into the later production model. The definitive AHB-443 entered production in 2703 and saw widespread distribution across SLDF forces and Great House militaries. Commanders with Ahab squadrons assigned to their task forces used the fighters to devastating effect against heavily fortified installations, and it was common for a full squadron to engage light and medium-class DropShips in a single coordinated pass.

Harvard Company went bankrupt in the early 3000s due to financial malfeasance, and production rights transferred to Bannock-Braigh Aerospace on Terra. BBA initially concentrated on manufacturing spare parts and minor upgrade packages rather than building new airframes in significant numbers. Critically, BBA sold its limited output exclusively to ComStar and deliberately neglected to provide parts or support to other military customers. As a result, Ahabs serving with the Great House militaries gradually fell into disuse and disrepair over the following decades. Many surviving airframes were downgraded to the earlier prototype configuration as advanced components like the NARC beacon became impossible to maintain.

Following the Word of Blake's seizure of Terra in 3058, Bannock-Braigh's longstanding ComStar contract became untenable, and the company's future shifted to its new masters. In 3061, BBA began manufacturing two new variants under Word of Blake direction. Though BBA was also producing parts and upgrade packages for the reconstituted SLDF and other House militaries during this period, the new Ahab variants were reserved exclusively for Blakist forces. The Free Worlds League fields the largest number of older Ahabs among the House militaries, with the League Admiralty assigning most of these heavy fighters to nadir and zenith jump point stations for system defense.

During the Jihad, Ahab squadrons featured prominently in some of the Word of Blake's most violent campaigns. Several squadrons proved instrumental in cracking the three main fortresses on Dieron during the Blakist siege of that world, helping turn the tide against the Combine's defenders. Newer variants appeared primarily among Protectorate Militia forces, and some mercenary commands employed by the Word of Blake were also observed fielding updated models alongside Protectorate units.
